author: root

silhouette.reason: Reference front silhouettes have dense rounded head/cheek masses and14px Brendan/May widths; v4 is12px wide, with narrower tapered head-to-neck and a small box torso. Its last5rows hold22opaque pixels versus48Brendan/40May, so the lower silhouette becomes exposed skin sticks instead of a compact dressed body.

anatomy.reason: Reference faces integrate ears/cheeks and2-row dark eyes into overlapping hat/hair/face clusters; Brendan eyes occupy y19/20, while v4 interior eyes are1px on one row(y16). V4 profile nose is an added point on a flat face wedge, and long bare skin columns below a one-row shorts band overstate shins rather than describing hips/thighs/ankles.

walking.reason: V4 does alternate limbs, but compared with all reference step pairs its upper body remains a near-identical box and forearms read as hinged pale rails. Bent rear shoe fixes semantic alternation without the reference clothing/hip/shoe cluster deformation and depth overlap. Side strides still change isolated skin columns and small shoe blocks more than a coherent dressed leg.

pixelCraft.reason: Reference pixels combine near-black contours, deliberate strong value ramps and connected planes for cap/hair/face/clothing/shoes. V4 spends several colors on closely spaced navy shades, with flat blue chest and orange/gold/red horizontal bands. Sparse isolated details and repeated rectangle clusters do not create comparable volume at1x.

identity.reason: The nominal cap/vest/gold-red bag is consistent, but reference costume details have shaped brims/hair breaks, front clothing structure and pack mass occlusion. V4 cap remains a generic slanted red patch above dark hair, vest a blue square, bag a gold rectangle with a red stripe. Color labels establish identity but not finished character design.

directionContinuity.reason: Heading and costume continuity remain valid across four directions. The references create more convincing front/profile/back volume, but v4 is not a direction-order or identity-swap failure.

loop.reason: All4decoded140ms frames and repeated idle form a consistent sequence without a file-level seam or unexplained root jump. This score concerns repeat continuity; it does not excuse the weak articulated gait captured by walking.

reviewIndependence: Same-model organizational/task separation only. No different-model or decorrelated aesthetic independence is claimed.
whyPriorScoreWasExcessive: I scored repairs relative to the old poor sprite and presence of cap/limb/bag features too generously, rather than calibrating completed native game craft against actual reference sprites.

I gave silhouette16/anatomy16/walking17/pixelCraft13/identity14 despite box torso, sparse skin-column lower body, one-row eyes and flat color bands; these visible defects conflict with the frozen finished-art anchors.
Hashes and two review records ensured traceability, not aesthetic truth; same-model root/critic organization did not provide decorrelated quality judgment.
requiredRedesign: Rebuild proportions from measured compact dressed silhouettes: fuller head/cheeks, shorter exposed shin region and connected shorts/trouser/shoe clusters.
Draw eye/face/hair/hat overlap as deliberate contrasting clusters rather than isolated dot eyes on a flat wedge.
Redesign entire front/side torso, hips and steps as overlapping cloth/limb masses with planted contact and compact swing, not bare-column rearrangements.
Reduce redundant navy colors, use meaningful dark contours/value ramps, and sculpt cap/vest/pack volumes as a coherent original design.
scope: Read-only reassessment plus requested report files. No original/reference artwork, source code, historical approval, gate or canonical store was changed.
measurementInterpretation: These measurements diagnose missing lower-body mass and mismatched proportion; they are not added numeric gate thresholds and do not require copying a reference silhouette or palette. Judge the redesigned original at native size under the same frozen rubric.
